events.title: Astronomer Tycho Brahe Is Born
events.description: Tycho Brahe was born into a Danish noble family in Scania, in present-day Sweden. He became one of history's most meticulous observers of the heavens. He charted the positions of stars and planets with a precision that was unmatched before the telescope.
events.significance: Brahe's detailed observations gave Johannes Kepler the data he needed to work out the laws of planetary motion. That helped lay the groundwork for modern astronomy.

events.title: George Washington Dies at Mount Vernon
events.description: The first President of the United States died at his Virginia estate at age 67, a few days after he fell ill. The young nation went into deep mourning.
events.significance: Washington had led the Continental Army to victory and then set precedents for the presidency, including voluntarily leaving office. His death marked the end of a founding era.

events.title: Alabama Becomes the 22nd State
events.description: Alabama was admitted to the Union as the 22nd state. It was part of a rapid westward expansion of the United States in the early 19th century.
events.significance: Its admission came during the debates over slavery's expansion that led to the Missouri Compromise. It shows how the question of slavery shaped the growth of the nation.

events.title: Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
events.description: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and four companions reached the geographic South Pole. They arrived about five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British expedition.
events.significance: It was one of the great achievements of the age of polar exploration. Amundsen's careful planning, skis and sled dogs became a model for later expeditions.

events.title: Mariner 2 Flies Past Venus
events.description: NASA's Mariner 2 spacecraft passed within roughly 34,000 kilometers (21,000 miles) of Venus. It collected data on the planet's atmosphere and temperature.
events.significance: This was the first successful close encounter with another planet by a spacecraft. It opened the era of robotic planetary exploration.
